newsitem.title: USA: Northeast needs fresh start -Conn. official.
newsitem.headline: Northeast needs fresh start -Conn. official.

text.p: Connecticut Attorney General Richard Blumenthal said Thursday that the retirement of Bernard M. Fox as chairman, president and chief executive of Northeast Utilities, would allow the company to get a "fresh start."
Northeast said earlier on Thursday that Fox planned to retire in the second half of this year.
The utility's troubled nuclear operation has been sharply criticized by federal regulators and citizens' watchdog groups for the past year.

"This decision (Fox's retirement) will allow Northeast Utilities to get a much-needed fresh start with new leadership at a particularly critical time for the electric industry in Connecticut," Blumenthal said in a statement.

"My hope is that the new leadership will recognize the critical importance of dealing candidly with the continuing effects of past mismanagement and embracing the future benefits of competition in the industry."
Northeast said its board was commencing a search for Fox's successor.
Blumenthal said earlier this month that he was disappointed in Northeast's proposal to delay full deregulation of Connecticut's electricity industry until 2003.
Blumenthal called the plan "woefully inadequate" and said he would like to see full deregulation in 1998 or soon after.

Blumenthal also said on Feb 11 that it was unacceptable for Connecticut ratepayers to be expected to finance the recovery of Northeast's "stranded costs" of up to $3 billion. Northeast's three Millstone nuclear power plants in Waterford, Conn., have been closed for safety reasons since March of last year.
